title: Eudiometry Analysis of Atmospheric O2 Percentage
author: Josep Grau
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baseiebe

steps.title: Prepare polysulfide solution
steps.instruction: Make 500 ml of polysulfide solution (enough for 4–5 measurements) by mixing the specified reagents, then boil for one hour while keeping the volume at 500 ml.

substeps.instruction: Weigh and combine 391.5 g distilled water, 74.5 g elemental sulfur (S), and 34 g calcium oxide (CaO) in a suitable container (these correspond to 78.3 % water, 14.9 % S, and 6.8 % CaO by weight).

Bring the mixture to a boil and maintain boiling for 1 hour. Replenish evaporated water as needed so that the total volume remains exactly 500 ml. The finished solution should appear deep orange, nearly red.

steps.title: Collect 100 ml atmospheric air
steps.instruction: Obtain exactly 100 ml of ambient air using a calibrated volumetric tube and a water bath.

substeps.instruction: Use a long volumetric tube (tube A) that is closed at one end and has a total volume larger than 100 ml.
Submerge tube A with its open side facing down into a water bath and allow air to escape until the trapped air volume inside the tube is exactly 100 ml.

steps.title: Combine air with polysulfide solution
steps.instruction: Introduce the 100 ml of collected air into a volume of polysulfide solution in a sealed flask, bubbling the air through the liquid.

substeps.instruction: Place at least 100 ml of the prepared polysulfide solution (excess is recommended) into a volumetric flask (flask B) that has a sealable narrow opening slightly larger than the diameter of tube A.
Quickly invert flask B (upside down) and submerge it in the water bath to minimise diffusion of polysulfide into the water.
At the same time, invert tube A and submerge it in the water bath, then bubble the air from tube A directly into flask B containing the polysulfide solution.

steps.title: Shake to complete reaction
steps.instruction: Vigorously shake the sealed flask to allow oxygen in the air to react with the polysulfide at the air‑liquid interface.

substeps.instruction: Shake vigorously for about 5 minutes (or longer if water has entered the flask) to generate as many bubbles as possible, ensuring complete reaction between O₂ and the polysulfide.

steps.title: Measure remaining air and calculate O₂
steps.instruction: Determine the volume of air that remains after reaction and compute the atmospheric oxygen percentage.

substeps.instruction: Submerge both vessels A and B in the water bath; ensure vessel A is completely filled with water.
Allow the air remaining in flask B to escape, bubbling it into vessel A (a funnel may help).
Record the final air volume in tube A; it should be less than the initial 100 ml (approximately 79 ml).
Calculate the oxygen concentration as 100 % – 79 % = 21 % v/v.
